title: Persistent exploration-exploitation failure regime in success-history DE
known: Success-history adaptation and population reduction are strong established mechanisms; later work reports premature convergence in higher dimensions and exploration imbalance on multimodal problems.
missing: A unified controlled map of when history-based adaptation plus population reduction crosses from beneficial exploitation to harmful diversity loss under dimension × modality × nonseparability × budget.
contradictory: Not yet established whether reported failures share one causal boundary across suites and implementations.
why_it_matters: Could support a transferable state-aware repair mechanism if existing remedies fail under controlled tests.
hypothesis: Search-state indicators predict a reproducible failure frontier better than iteration count alone.
minimal_test: SHADE and L-SHADE vs established repair variants under equal evaluations across controlled dimensions, multimodality and rotations; track diversity, success rate, parameter memory and evaluations-to-target.
